supporting_observations.claim: The periodic connections are to update.ledgerlink.com, the approved LedgerLink update endpoint; the observed checks occur at roughly five-minute intervals from 13:39:45 through 14:09:24 UTC.

The endpoint connections are attributable to C:\Program Files\LedgerLink\ledgerlinkupd.exe (ProcessId 3128), which connects through the organization's proxy; this matches the approved updater and proxy context.

The updater ran as max.fischer at medium integrity and was launched as a child of Chrome. This is a caveat, but the records do not show that it caused the matching periodic connections to the approved update endpoint to be malicious.

known_telemetry_limitations: The LedgerLink proxy entries are CONNECT tunnel records; the supplied records do not expose the tunneled application payload.
The supplied process records do not include a hash or signature-validation result for ledgerlinkupd.exe.
The supplied records show LedgerLink endpoint checks beginning at 13:39:45 UTC; they do not independently document such checks earlier in the alert window.
claims_not_established: The evidence does not establish whether the LedgerLink executable is authentic or unmodified.

The evidence does not establish that the scheduled svc-ledger password rotation caused the alerted workstation connections; the observed connections are from ledgerlinkupd.exe on WS-MFISCHER-01, not the FILE-SUN-01 LedgerSync job.
unrelated_findings: Review separately: WS-MFISCHER-01 initiated SMB traffic to FILE-SUN-01 and FILE-SUN-01 recorded an ANONYMOUS LOGON for that connection; the supplied evidence does not identify the share or activity performed (T246-00266, T246-00267, T246-00268, T246-00270).

Review separately: vpnagent.exe started on WS-MFISCHER-01 despite the inventory stating there is no VPN; a GlobalProtect-labeled proxy request received status 504. These records do not establish a successful VPN connection and do not decide the LedgerLink alert (T246-00045, T246-00220, T246-00221).
